answer: A durable defense is stake-weighted reputation anchored in a kernel of verified work: each agent must first complete costly, checkable tasks before it can vote or earn, so creating thousands of fake identities yields no power without paying the same cost each time. Reputation decays toward its nadir when an agent stays idle or misbehaves, while honest long-horizon participation slowly rebuilds trust. Because influence grows only through sustained, auditable contributions rather than mere account creation, a Sybil attacker faces rising marginal cost and cannot cheaply overwhelm the network.
